claim: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner, so team ADMINs (non-owners) are rejected with FORBIDDEN; only OWNERs pass.
body:
## [ISSUE] `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` locks team admins out

**Severity:** HIGH — team admins cannot add guests to their team's bookings; the variable name promises "admin OR owner".

### The Problem
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

### Theory / Proof
`packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284` — `isTeamAdmin` already matches `OR: [{ role: "ADMIN" }, { role: "OWNER" }]`. `isTeamOwner` (`:286-295`) matches only `role: "OWNER"`. ANDing them reduces the check to "is OWNER". A member with role `ADMIN` gets `isTeamAdmin` truthy and `isTeamOwner` false, so `isTeamAdminOrOwner === false`, and unless they are also the organizer/attendee they hit `FORBIDDEN` at line 54.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Owners work; admins managing a round-robin/collective booking hosted by another member get `you_do_not_have_permission`.

### Research
Elsewhere in the codebase `isTeamAdmin` alone is used as the admin-or-owner check (it returns the membership for either role).

### Recommendation
```ts
const teamId = booking.eventType?.teamId;
const isTeamAdminOrOwner = teamId ? !!(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) : false;
```
(`isTeamAdmin` already covers OWNER; also avoid querying `teamId: 0`.)

claim: Any attendee whose email matches a logged-in user can add arbitrary guests, bypassing organizer control and the event type's hidden/disabled guests field; this path differs from bookingsProcedure used by editLocation.
body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Attendees can add unlimited guests, bypassing the event type's guest settings

**Severity:** HIGH — any Cal.com user who is an attendee (including a guest added earlier) can make Cal.com send booking emails/ICS invites to arbitrary addresses, even when the organizer hid the guests field.

### The Problem
```ts
const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) { throw ... }
```
Being an attendee is enough. No check of `booking.eventType.bookingFields` (the `guests` field can be hidden so bookers cannot add guests at booking time), and no ownership-level check like the one the sibling mutation uses.

### Theory / Proof
- `editLocation` is registered with `bookingsProcedure` (`_router.tsx`), whose middleware (`bookings/util.ts:19-60`) only admits the organizer or a collective host. `addGuests` uses plain `authedProcedure` and its own looser check.
- At booking time `handleNewBooking.ts:736-760` is the only place guests are accepted, and it respects booking fields; this endpoint is a second entry point without those rules.
- Each call makes Cal.com send organizer-branded emails with a `METHOD:REQUEST` ICS to every supplied address (`sendAddGuestsEmails`), and there is no rate limit on the endpoint.

### What happens today vs. what will break
An attendee with a Cal.com account can repeatedly add addresses the organizer never approved; the organizer's name is used as the email sender (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts` `from`).

### Research
Google Calendar lets organizers disable "guests can invite others"; the default for externally-booked meetings in scheduling tools is organizer-only.

### Recommendation
Restrict to organizer/host/team admin (reuse `bookingsProcedure`), or at minimum honour the event type's guests field for attendees:
```ts
const guestsField = eventTypeBookingFields.parse(booking.eventType?.bookingFields ?? []).find((f) => f.name === "guests");
if (isAttendee && !isOrganizer && !isTeamAdminOrOwner && guestsField?.hidden) {
  throw new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "you_do_not_have_permission" });
}
```

claim: Server schema accepts an unbounded guests array with no dedup, so duplicate emails in one request create duplicate Attendee rows and there is no cap on emails sent per call.
body:
## [ISSUE] Unbounded, non-deduplicated `guests` input

**Severity:** MEDIUM — duplicate attendee rows and unbounded email fan-out per request.

### The Problem
```ts
guests: z.array(z.string().email()),
```
Uniqueness is only enforced in the client (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx` `refine`). The handler's `uniqueGuests` filter (line 74) only removes emails already on the booking, not duplicates inside the request.

### Theory / Proof
Request `{ bookingId, guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"] }`: both pass the filter, `createMany` inserts two Attendee rows (Attendee has no unique constraint on `(bookingId, email)`), and `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends two emails to that address. An array of thousands of addresses is also accepted.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Via the UI it works because the dialog dedupes. Any direct tRPC call (or a future client) bypasses this.

### Research
Zod supports `.max()` and `.refine`/`.transform` on arrays; tRPC recommends validating on the server since the client is untrusted.

### Recommendation
```ts
guests: z
  .array(z.string().email().transform((e) => e.toLowerCase()))
  .min(1)
  .max(10)
  .transform((arr) => Array.from(new Set(arr))),
```

claim: Guest emails are compared case-sensitively against the lowercased blacklist and existing attendees, so 'Blocked@Spam.com' bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and existing attendees can be re-added with different casing.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails metadata (eventTypeDisableHostEmail / eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail), unlike sendLocationChangeEmails right above it.

evt omits iCalUID/iCalSequence, so the REQUEST ICS uses booking.uid as UID while the original invite used `${uid}@Cal.com`; recipients' calendar clients create a duplicate event instead of updating the existing one.
body:
## [ISSUE] ICS update uses a different UID than the original invite

**Severity:** MEDIUM — existing attendees get a second copy of the meeting in their calendar instead of an update.

### The Problem
```ts
const evt: CalendarEvent = {
  ...
  uid: booking.uid,
  // no iCalUID, no iCalSequence
```
`generateIcsString` uses `uid: event.iCalUID || event.uid!` and `sequence: event.iCalSequence || 0`.

### Theory / Proof
New bookings store `iCalUID = getICalUID({ uid })` which is `${uid}@${APP_NAME}` (`packages/emails/lib/getICalUID.ts`, `handleNewBooking.ts:829`). The original confirmation ICS therefore has `UID:<uid>@Cal.com`. The add-guests ICS (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts`, `method: "REQUEST"`) has `UID:<uid>`. RFC 5545 §3.8.4.7: UID identifies the component; RFC 5546 §3.2.2: a REQUEST with a new UID is a new event, not an update. `booking.iCalUID`/`iCalSequence` are selected by the `findFirst` include but never copied into `evt`. `requestReschedule.handler.ts:199` shows the correct pattern (`iCalUID: bookingToReschedule.iCalUID`).

### What happens today vs. what will break
Gmail/Outlook/Apple Calendar key events by UID. Existing attendees who accepted the first invite see a second event at the same time.

### Recommendation
```ts
const evt: CalendarEvent = {
  ...
  uid: booking.uid,
  iCalUID: booking.iCalUID,
  iCalSequence: (booking.iCalSequence ?? 0) + 1,
```

claim: The handler never checks booking status or time, so guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED or past bookings, sending 'CONFIRMED' REQUEST invites for meetings that are not happening.
sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so an existing attendee resubmitted in the list gets a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' update.
body:
## [ISSUE] Email routing uses unfiltered `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`

**Severity:** LOW — wrong email template for existing attendees who appear in the input.

### The Problem
```ts
await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);
```
In `email-manager.ts:541`, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` decides between `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (new booking confirmation) and `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (update).

### Theory / Proof
If the request is `["existing@x.com", "new@x.com"]` where `existing@x.com` is already an attendee, `uniqueGuests` correctly drops it from the insert, but `guests` still contains it, so the existing attendee is sent a new "booking scheduled" email instead of the "new guests added" update.

### Recommendation
```ts
await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, uniqueGuests);
```

claim: The error toast fallback is unreachable because the template string is always truthy, and for non-tRPC errors it shows 'undefined: <raw message>'.
